elements.name: page-3-text
elements.title: Third Spaces
elements.description:
The concept of "third places" was coined by sociologist Ray Oldenburg in 1989 to describe informal places beyond the first place (home) and second place (work), where people voluntarily gather and build community. In academic institutions, third spaces refer to informal environments beyond classrooms, comprising non-classroom spaces and circulation spaces, where students choose to spend time without a formal agenda.

While students have differing preferences, they can benefit from these three types of third spaces:
1. For self – spaces for self-regulation, reflection, and spending time alone
2. For peer interactions - spaces that support social interaction and strengthen friendships
3. For school community interactions and events – spaces that create a strong sense of school community and belonging

This section aims to identify the qualities students value in EJC's third spaces.

elements.name: question4
elements.title: Pedestrian Circulation
elements.description:
In schools, where large groups of students frequently transition between different areas, it is important to consider the quality of circulation spaces and how they affect the ease and comfort of movement.

This section assesses the quality of circulation design in EJC.

elements.name: circulation-1
elements.title: Please rate the extent to which you agree with the following statements.

rows.text: Travelling between spaces within the school feels smooth and efficient.
Besides travelling between spaces, I often use the corridors for informal social interactions, discussions, and/or other student activities.
It is acceptable for me that lifts only stop at selected floors to improve efficiency, even if it means taking the stairs afterwards.
Lifts and stairs are conveniently located.

elements.name: circulation-2
elements.title: What factors may influence your decision to take the stairs rather than the lift?
elements.description: Tick all that apply.
choices: Lifts do not serve the floors that I am going to
More direct way to my destination

elements.name: circulation-3
elements.title: Please rate the extent to which you agree with the following statements on the courtyard.

rows.text: The design of the courtyard makes travelling between floors enjoyable.
The staircases within the courtyard are conveniently located for travelling between floors.
The greenery along corridors and elevated gardens in the courtyard contributes to a pleasant school environment.
The openness of the multi-level courtyard encourages spontaneous interactions with other students.
The size and proportion of the courtyard makes me feel more connected to the wider school community despite being a high-rise building.

elements.name: question7
elements.title: Greenery & Green Spaces
elements.description:
A distinctive feature of EJC is its proximity to Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park. The design of the campus also integrates green elements that extend the park experience into the school. 

This section assesses how students perceive the greenery in and around the campus in a high-rise setting, providing insights into the role of greenery in supporting student learning.

elements.name: green-1
elements.title: Please rate the extent to which you agree with the following statements on the greenery in and around EJC.

rows.text: The greenery in and around the school contributes positively to my school experience.
I enjoy seeing greenery from different areas and levels of the school.
Greenery integrated within the school makes travelling between spaces more pleasant.

elements.name: green-2
elements.title: Please rate the extent to which you agree with the following statements on the adjacency to Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park.

rows.text: I visit or pass through the Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, for any purposes, as part of my school day.
The direct bridge connection between EJC and the park encourages me to visit the park.
I enjoy the "School in a Park" setting, which is unique to EJC.

elements.name: question11
elements.title: Integration with Marymount Community Club
elements.description:
EJC is the first junior college to be integrated with a community club (CC) under one roof.

This section assesses how Eunoians engage with the spaces and people within Marymount Community Club, providing insights into how effectively the school and Community Club function as a mixed-use development.
